svg.title: The same two conditioning laws, used on purpose
svg.desc: Top: anxiety plotted against time for the two exposure routes. Systematic desensitisation climbs a hierarchy while the patient stays relaxed, so anxiety stays low throughout; flooding presents the worst item at once and the patient waits out a single large spike. Both end at the same place, but flooding is harder to tolerate and more people drop out. Middle left: the three-term contingency with the operant techniques hung on it — antecedents are handled by prompting and fading, behaviour by shaping and chaining, consequences by reinforcement, extinction and response cost. Middle right: the extinction burst, a temporary worsening before the decline, with the warning that giving in during the burst converts the behaviour to an intermittent schedule and makes it harder to shift. Bottom: the token economy as a two-step exchange, and the ladder of least restrictive alternatives that ethics requires be climbed from the bottom.
svg.text: The same two conditioning laws, used on purpose
Classical techniques re-pair a stimulus; operant techniques re-arrange consequences
Two routes to the same extinction
systematic desensitisation: relaxed the whole way
imaginal first, then in vivo — real contact generalises better
negative reinforcement is still reinforcement: it raises behaviour
Expect it to get worse first
give in here and you have just taught
an intermittent schedule — the hardest kind to undo
Climb from the bottom, and only if you must
consent, assent, and review before anything aversive
